The U.S. is reestablishing military ties with Venezuela.
Defense Secretary Pete Hexeth announced the agreement during a visit to Caracas,

country since the U.S. military raid that removed Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro from power.
A Maduro ally took over, though her term formally expired in July,
and no date has been set for a new presidential election unnerving many Venezuelans about the
U.S.'s priorities in their country. Congressman Hakeem Jeffries has been nominated for House
Speaker of the Democrats taking control of Congress in January. Here's NPR's Jorge Grisales.
House Democrats voted during a closed-door meeting 251 to 11 in support of Hakeem Jeffries'
nomination. Afterwards, the current House Minority Leader told reporters his caucus will work to
deliver for the American people. Our job is to fight MAGA extremism, not each other, to fight
MAGA extremism, and to get big things done. Several incoming more left-wing House members
who did not support Jeffries' bid said they're still pushing for a more aggressive agenda to
address affordability, immigration, and other issues. The House floor will hold its vote for
Speaker on the first day of the new Congress next year on January 3. Claudia Ritzalis, NPR News,
the Capitol. At yesterday's earnings call, the chair of NVIDIA's board ruled out Jensen Wong's
reinstatement as CEO despite pressure from Wong's allies. NPR's John Ruich says Wong's the subject
of multiple investigations involving his connection to a suspected Chinese spy. There are allegations
that companies like the one run by the Chinese woman that Jensen Wong reportedly had an affair
with were helping China get a hold of banned ships that could potentially point to violations
of U.S. export controls. That's NPR's John Ruich reporting. Homeland Security Secretary Mark
Wayne Mullins testifying on Capitol Hill at a hearing about the recent spate of global tech
outages arguing there's no evidence they resulted from cyberattacks, but AI is a factor. NPR's
Windsor Johnson looks at the latest disruption to Apple and reporting on how AI may be pushing
companies to fix security flaws faster. Apple says an internal update disrupted iCloud and
Apple Pay. The outage is the latest in a string of disruptions affecting the FAA, United Airlines,
Microsoft, Chase, Zelle and the National Security Agency. Laurie Craner, a cybersecurity researcher
at Carnegie Mellon University, points to the pressure to fix security flaws. Things are moving
faster. We need to upgrade faster. We need to protect against threats discovered by AI.
So there may be more of a flurry of upgrading, which is causing outages when the upgrades are
not being done carefully. That's NPR's Windsor Johnston. Globally, Muslims are expected to
outnumber Christians by the year 2035. NPR's Jason DeRose reports that's among the findings
of a new study on religious trends from Pew Research. Pew projects that by the year 2070,
Christians will decline to less than half of the US population, though they'll remain the country's
largest single religious group. At the same time, religiously unaffiliated people will rise to just
over 40 percent, mostly due to people leaving Christianity. Currently, Judaism is the largest
non-Christian religion in the US, but researchers say that by 2070, Jews will be outnumbered by both
Muslims and Hindus in this country if recent demographic trends continue. Globally, Pew projects
that more than half of the world's Christians will live in sub-Saharan Africa by the year 2070,
largely due to higher birth rates there. Jason DeRose, NPR News.
David Beckham's luxury fragrances have allegedly been found on sale at a British discount store
and a gas station bargain bin, and the soccer-slash-style icon is not having it.
